newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian shares gain, led by banks.
newsitem.headline: Estonian shares gain, led by banks.

text.p: Estonian shares gained on Monday and dealers said foreign investor interest remained strong which supported several banking stocks.
Leading banks Hansapank and Union Bank were firm, with Hansapank ending above the key 200 kroon level.
"Interest from local and foreign investors is still quite strong and looks like it will stay that way," one analyst said.
The Tallinn stock exchange index gained 0.93 percent to close at 201.95 percent on a turnover of 32.8 million kroons on the official list.
Union Bank shares were most traded on turnover of 8.9 million kroons to close one kroon higher at 42.95 kroons.
"Local market makers were buying strongly this morning and this was supported by more interest from Helsinki later in the day," one dealer said.
Union Bank's shares in Helsinki rose 0.40 markka to 16.40 markka on volume of 2,000.
Leading blue chip Hansapank broke through the 200 kroon mark again and ended above that level to finish at 200.80 kroons, up 2.60 kroons on trade of 8.6 million kroons.
Savings Bank also turned over eight million kroons of shares to register total trade of 8.2 million as it closed 0.35 kroons higher on 95.35 kroons.
Among other stocks, Forekspank registered trade of 3.2 million kroons to remain stable on 148.50 kroons.
Tallinna Pank eased 0.40 kroons to close on 61.35 kroons with a trade of 3.2 million kroons of shares.
It earlier announced it would boost its share capital with the issue of one million shares with a nominal value of 10 kroons each.
The over-the-counter market turned over 6.6 million kroons of shares.
Rakvere meat plant turnover of 2.9 million kroons to close 0.05 firmer at 13.50 kroons.
Saku Brewery, which earlier released figures to show a slightly lower 1996 profit, was down one kroon to 49 kroons on trade of 1.9 million kroons.
Norma plastics maker was 0.40 kroons stronger to end trading at 58.60 kroons on volume of 1.1 million kroons of shares.
